newsitem.title: CANADA: CanOxy wins battle to take over Wascana Energy.
newsitem.headline: CanOxy wins battle to take over Wascana Energy.

text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. emerged the winner in a C$2 billion ($1.44 billion) battle for Wascana Energy Inc. on Wednesday after rival bidder Talisman Energy Inc. bowed out of the race.

Calgary-based Talisman, which opened the bidding for Wascana in February with a C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion) cash and stock offer, said it would not put more money on the table because it could not see the extra value in Wascana's assets.

Talisman's stock price was battered by investors after its bid and the company could not justify issuing more shares or assuming more debt to boost its offer, Talisman Chief Executive Jim Buckee said.

CanOxy, which entered as white knight for Regina, Saskatchewan-based Wascana with a C$20.50 ($14.76) a share all-cash offer in March, is now poised to enter the ranks of Canada's top three oil and gas producers. Its bid expires on Monday.

Under the friendly merger deal, the richest in Canada's oil patch since 1994, Wascana will become a wholly owned unit of Calgary-based CanOxy, which agreed to keep the former Saskatchewan government-owned oil producer's head office in Regina as spelled out in provincial legislation.
CanOxy, 30 percent-owned by Occidental Petroleum Corp. of Los Angeles, also agreed to maintain Wascana's employment levels in the western Canadian province.
CanOxy and Talisman investors reacted positively to the move on Wednesday, driving up both firms' share prices.
Talisman shares climbed C$1.10 to C$40.40 in Toronto The stock had fallen by $7 from its high during the early stages of the bid process.
It had offered C$18.50 cash ($13.32) or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share.
CanOxy rose C$2.10 to a year high of C$27.20. Wascana was down C10 cents to C$20.45 in Toronto.

"What you're seeing in the market today is a vote of confidence in this transaction," CanOxy Vice-President Charlie Fischer told Reuters. "The feedback that we've had right from the time we made our offer was people thought this was a very good match for us."
CanOxy said Wascana, with its extensive heavy oil production in Western Canada, would provide much-needed balance to its numerous international high-risk exploration plays.

Talisman's Buckee on Wednesday described as "offensive" his firm's being shut out of Wascana's confidential data room after CanOxy announced its bid and he suggested legal action might be in the offing.
Wascana had said Talisman needed to raise its bid before getting data access.

"Obviously, we were a bona fide bidder. We stated that we would pay more for proven value and we continue to believe that we would have been the best able to exploit these assets," Buckee said in a conference call. "There is a legal case here waiting to be tested."
